# Scarcity in an age of AI abundance

> This is a paper record, not a replication package: the paper is theoretical and has no data and
> no computation to reproduce. The paper argues that AI can make many goods and services cheap to
> produce (AI technological abundance, ATA) without making an essential standard of living broadly
> affordable (AI economic abundance, AEA), because scarcity and its rents move to five layers:
> physical resources, infrastructure, capabilities, institutions and jurisdictions. The record
> holds the paper's definitions, the five layers with the prediction for each, the model, and Table
> 1 as data, all read out of the manuscript source. One added page, which goes beyond the article,
> says how each prediction could be found wrong. The manuscript is in paper/.

Replication package by Agisilaos Papadogiannis (https://github.com/apapadogiannis).
Forthcoming in Asian Review of Political Economy (2027). Preprint: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5924462
Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/ai-abundance  Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24441153
Version 1.0.1, released 2026-11-22. A package is a fixed record: it changes only by a new
release, and a release that changes a reported number gets a new major version.
This file is written for AI agents and other programs. People should start at the README.

## Coverage

- Table 1 of the paper: 24 actors and industries in five panels, with the sign of each of the five
  layers' contribution to the actor's rent income and the net sign. 144 signs.
- The five layers of scarcity: what each holds and the one-sentence prediction the paper makes for
  it.
- The three central claims and seven definitions, in the paper's own words.
- The model: Equations 1 to 6, Definition 1, Proposition 1 and its proof, with the mathematics in
  LaTeX, and a glossary of 21 symbols.
- Beyond the article: 11 tests, each with a measure, the kind of public source it can be read from,
  the outcome that would count against the paper and what would not. Two baselines, 2022 and 2026;
  readings on data for 2027 and for 2032; the verdict is taken on the change from 2026 to 2032. Ten
  of the 24 rows of Table 1 are used by a test.
- The three figures of the paper are diagrams and have no data.

## What this adds over reading the paper or recomputing

1. The table as data. Each of the 144 signs (120 layer signs and 24 net signs) can be looked up by
   actor and column, and each actor has an identifier (A1 to E4) that the tests use. When the
   record was made, the signs were compared once with the table in the journal's proof of the
   article, and all 144 agreed; that comparison is not part of the check, because the proof is not
   in this repository.
2. A statement of what in the paper can and cannot be wrong. Proposition 1 is an existence claim
   proved by construction, so no observation can count against it. The article calls its condition
   (6) falsifiable: that condition can be checked for a given economy, which is a different thing.
   The layer predictions and five pairs of rows of Table 1 can be wrong, and outputs/tests.csv says
   by what measure and by when; beyond/README.md says how the verdict is taken and where the tests
   are weak. The article itself gives no date and no measure.
3. The paper's own limits, kept with the content: the table's caption says its entries are
   schematic and conjectural, 'not forecasts', and 'may not materialize'. The record repeats this
   wherever the signs are described.
4. A separation of what is the article and what is not. Six tables hold the article's own signs and
   passages. In them the record supplies only the row identifiers, the column names, the names of
   the six equations, the scores, the choice of the seven defining passages and the column that
   says which tests use a row. outputs/symbols.csv is a glossary written for this record from the
   article's definitions. outputs/tests.csv, and the folder beyond/, go beyond the article.
5. The signs, the passages and the equations are read out of the manuscript source by a script, so
   none of them is typed. The script fails if the manuscript does not have 24 actors in five
   panels, the five layer columns in order, five layers and six equations, if a symbol of the
   glossary does not occur in the manuscript, or if a test refers to a row or a layer that does not
   exist.
6. The results are stored as they were when the paper's numbers were taken from them. A check
   reruns the code on the stored data and compares every stored result file with the fresh one,
   number by number (relative tolerance 1e-9; text and whole numbers exactly). It runs on every
   change and once a month, and the badge in the README shows the last run.

## Result tables

One CSV file each in outputs/. The columns of each are described in outputs/results.json, under `tables`.

- outputs/table1.csv (24 rows): Table 1 of the paper, one row per actor or industry: the expected
  direction of each layer's contribution to rent income, and the net direction. Schematic and
  conjectural; the article says the entries are not forecasts.
- outputs/table1_signs.csv (144 rows): The same table with one row per actor and column, for
  filtering: 24 actors times five layers and the net column.
- outputs/layers.csv (5 rows): The five layers of scarcity, in the article's words.
- outputs/claims.csv (3 rows): The three central claims, as listed in the introduction.
- outputs/definitions.csv (7 rows): Seven terms of the paper, each with the passage of the article
  that defines it.
- outputs/model.csv (9 rows): The model of the section 'A compact mathematical formulation': six
  equations, the definition of AEA, the proposition and its proof.
- outputs/symbols.csv (21 rows): Glossary of the symbols. Written for this record from the
  article's definitions; not a passage of the article.
- outputs/tests.csv (11 rows): Beyond the article: for each prediction, how it could be found
  wrong. Baselines 2022 and 2026; first reading on data for 2027, final reading on data for 2032.
  No reading has been taken.

## Files

- outputs/results.json: a description of the eight record tables and the meaning of every column.
  The content itself is in the CSV files. It holds a description of 8 result tables, and under
  `package` the paper, the identifiers, the version, the licence and the citation. Start here.
- outputs/table1.csv: for the table. One row per actor.
- outputs/tests.csv: for what would count against the paper. The page beyond/README.md explains the
  dates, how the verdict is taken and the limits of the tests.
- paper/manuscript.pdf, paper/manuscript.tex: the paper, author's version of the accepted text.
- data/symbols.csv, beyond/tests.csv: the two files written by hand. The script checks them; it
  copies the first into outputs/ and joins the second to the passages and signs it refers to.

Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-abundance/main/<path>, for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-abundance/main/outputs/results.json

## How to read the figures

- A sign in Table 1 is the direction the paper expects for the change in an actor's rent income
  from one layer (the product of the actor's share of that layer and the layer's rent). The article
  calls the cells qualitative. ++ and -- mark a stronger change than + and -; the article gives no
  size. 0 means no change or roughly none (the text says 'roughly neutral' and 'near zero'); it
  does not mean missing.
- The double minus is written -- in the files. The journal prints it as two minus signs.
- The net column is, in the article's words, the implied direction of the change in the actor's
  total rent income, which is the sum of the five layer components. The sizes of those components
  are not given, so the net cannot be recomputed from the signs, and the scores must not be added
  up: for A5 the layers are 0, ++, +, ++, ++ and the net is ++; for C1 they are 0, -, -, 0, 0 and
  the net is -.
- The scores 2, 1, 0, -1, -2 in outputs/table1_signs.csv only encode the signs for sorting and
  filtering. They are not on an interval scale.
- The table says 'post-AI' without a date. The article's regime boundary, Point A, is a threshold
  of deployment and not a year.
- The household rows (D1, D2) are read through household claims on layer rents and transfers, not
  through direct ownership, as the article says.
- A positive sign can come from a higher layer rent, a larger share of it, or both. The table does
  not say which.
- The predictions in outputs/layers.csv are quoted from the article. The measures and dates in
  outputs/tests.csv and the verdict rules in beyond/README.md are not from the article: they were
  set by the author for this record on 22 November 2026. Measured from 2022 the tests are not
  blind: four of the five years to the first reading had passed when they were written. The second
  baseline, 2026, is the year they were written, and the verdict is taken on the change from 2026
  to 2032.
- A test on two rows of Table 1 says which of the two did better. It does not test the level the
  table gives either row.
- A passage in outputs/definitions.csv is cut out of the article as it stands. It can be a phrase
  and not a sentence, and it can refer to text before it ('these mechanisms' in the passage on
  Point A are the four domains of cost compression). The formal definition of AEA is Definition 1
  in outputs/model.csv. The article says 'broad affordability' in words and 'every household' in
  Definition 1.
- Cite the article. Its DOI is https://doi.org/10.1007/s44216-026-00090-y. The citation below gives
  the address of the preprint, which is where the text can be read until the article appears.
- Mathematics is kept in LaTeX: R_{2,t} is the rent of layer 2 at date t. outputs/symbols.csv
  explains each symbol.
- The title is written as the journal prints it, in sentence case. Earlier versions of the preprint
  used 'Scarcity in an Age of AI Abundance'.

## Do not use this for

- A forecast of returns, margins or prices for any industry or company. The table's entries are
  qualitative conjectures and the article says they are not forecasts.
- Evidence that the predictions hold. No test in this record has been read against data.
- An estimate of the size of any rent, of the ownership shares, or of the cost of the reference
  bundle. The model has no calibrated parameter.
- A date for AI technological abundance or a view on whether artificial general intelligence is
  feasible. The paper takes no position on either.
- Investment advice.
